svg.aria-label: Block diagram of mlc_cache_top: two L1 controllers, the L1 to L2 arbiter, the L2 controller, the width adapter, the L3 controller, the AXI4 fill engine, the memory model and the bound checkers

path.title: port 1: fill read or store forward (dn_req_*)
wr_fwd: pending store, drained with priority
store hit with L2 busy, or write-allocate fill done
l3_req_*: wdata = L2 line, wstrb all ones
ARREADY, AWREADY, WREADY, R beats, B
observes the same rules at L3

g.text: write-through; the ports have no writes
a hit answers in the accept cycle
store hit: array updated and forwarded
store miss: fill, merge, then forward
no eviction state: lines are never dirty
req_ready is low during a miss and while
a forwarded store is still pending
a read miss sets busy; the reply goes
to the owner; L2 is shown nothing meanwhile
a read hit is answered in its accept cycle
free way first, otherwise the PLRU victim
half = req_addr[5] selects the L2 half
a write-back is one posted half-line write
wstrb all ones; no state, no clock
the same FSM as L2, WR_BYTES = 32
write slot = one L2 line (half an L3 line)
a dirty victim goes to memory over AXI4
IDLE · AR · R · RESP · WR · B
or a missing or early RLAST
